title: Taoyuan's AI sound cameras locate a white BMW that had been roaring down Jieshou Road at night, within a day of residents' complaint
summary: Taoyuan's AI sound cameras pinpointed a white BMW noise car the day after residents complained; officers caught it on 23 April 2025.
account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. A Noise Control Act fine of up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order are to follow.
purpose: The bureau places mobile AI sound cameras on main roads and residential streets to collect noise data. Combined with complaint data, this gives the time and place of illegally modified noisy vehicles. Locating this car was that purpose.
system: AI sound camera equipment (AI聲音照相) of the Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) project, part of the bureau's network of 'improved mobile sound cameras' (改良式移動聲音照相)
deployer: Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection (桃園市政府環境保護局), with the Taoyuan City Police Department for the stop
taxonomy_note: The residents' good, noise abatement, has no type; the documented gain is the bureau's one-day enforcement cycle.

ratings.reason: Residents on Jieshou Road had written that the car's late-night passes seriously affected their quality of life and sleep. They saw it identified and referred for a modification review and fine within a day. The reports do not document whether the noise ceased afterwards.

The bureau closed one complaint in 24 hours and used the case to publicize its sound-camera enforcement. Its claim that the cameras “greatly raise the success rate” of tracking noise vehicles comes without figures.

ai_role.statement: The bureau's own description is the only account of the system's contribution. The task force placed AI sound camera equipment at the relevant locations on the night of the complaint. Analysis of the noise data with the complaint reports gave the car's haunts and times. Environmental and police officers then found it near Daxing Road on 23 April. The sources do not say how the cameras tie noise to a vehicle. They report no decibel reading. They give no counterfactual for how long a conventional patrol would have taken. The stop, the referral and the pending penalty were the officers' work.

produced_by: A complaint that named the road and the time window (late night on Jieshou Road). This told the task force where to place the cameras the same night.
Mobile AI sound cameras already in the bureau's inventory under the Quiet Taoyuan project. Deployment did not wait on procurement.
A standing environmental-police joint enforcement arrangement that could put officers at the predicted place and time on 23 April.
must_hold: The target must be a repeat offender with a pattern. The method matches noise data against complaint times and places, and cannot catch a one-off pass.
Officers must be free to intercept on the night the analysis points to. The cameras locate; they do not stop.
A legal basis for the follow-up: here the Noise Control Act (fine up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order). Also the Road Traffic Management and Penalty Act (up to NT$24,000 for a removed muffler).

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as benefit created or restored as the classifier proposed: the AI located a car that had already been causing the nuisance, and the dated benefit is a one-day enforcement cycle rather than the prevention of a specific future harm. Every report reproduces the Department of Environmental Protection's 29 April statement, with photographs credited to the bureau; the Liberty Times piece carries its own reporter's byline and quotes the director, 顏己喨. The bureau's own press release could not be retrieved (dep.tycg.gov.tw did not respond and tycg.gov.tw sits behind anti-DDoS protection), and the UDN link on the Monitor returns 404. Corrections to the Monitor summary: the fine had not been imposed at the time of reporting; the reports say the car will subsequently be fined under the Noise Control Act (up to NT$3,600) after referral to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. “BMW” appears in the Taoyuan E-News and Guan Media versions; the Liberty Times and Taiwan Hot News say only “white noise car”. The Monitor's “Economic/Property” harm to the general public is the nuisance the car caused, not anything the AI did. Dated to the stop on 23 April 2025; the complaint arrived on the night of 22 April; the Monitor's ID date (29 April) is the press coverage.
Added what the benefit is measured against, what happened since, the value as stated from the cited sources.
Country of the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: a rating reason, account, purpose, the replication conditions, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.

fields.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. A Noise Control Act fine of up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order are to follow.

The Monitor's “Economic/Property” harm to the general public is the nuisance the car caused, not anything the AI did. Dated to the stop on 23 April 2025; the complaint arrived on the night of 22 April; the Monitor's ID date (29 April) is the press coverage.

Country of the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.

produced_by: A complaint that named the road and the time window (late night on Jieshou Road). This told the task force where to place the cameras the same night.

must_hold: The target must be a repeat offender with a pattern. The method matches noise data against complaint times and places, and cannot catch a one-off pass.

A legal basis for the follow-up: here the Noise Control Act (fine up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order). Also the Road Traffic Management and Penalty Act (up to NT$24,000 for a removed muffler).

fields.summary: Taoyuan's AI sound cameras pinpointed a white BMW noise car the day after residents complained; officers caught it on 23 April 2025.
fields.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. A Noise Control Act fine of up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order are to follow.

fields.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. A Noise Control Act fine of up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order are to follow.

produced_by: A complaint that named the road and the time window (late night on Jieshou Road). This told the task force where to place the cameras the same night.
Mobile AI sound cameras already in the bureau's inventory under the Quiet Taoyuan project. Deployment did not wait on procurement.
A standing environmental-police joint enforcement arrangement that could put officers at the predicted place and time on 23 April.
must_hold: The target must be a repeat offender with a pattern. The method matches noise data against complaint times and places, and cannot catch a one-off pass.
Officers must be free to intercept on the night the analysis points to. The cameras locate; they do not stop.
A legal basis for the follow-up: here the Noise Control Act (fine up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order). Also the Road Traffic Management and Penalty Act (up to NT$24,000 for a removed muffler).
